short: British politician and philanthropist who led the parliamentary campaign to abolish the slave trade.
full:
William Wilberforce entered Parliament in 1780 and soon underwent a profound evangelical conversion that redirected his political career towards humanitarian causes. Supported by a network of activists known as the Clapham Sect, he became the parliamentary figurehead of the abolitionist movement, introducing anti-slavery motions year after year in the face of entrenched opposition from West Indian planters.

His relentless two-decade campaign culminated in the passing of the Slave Trade Act in 1807, which legally abolished the slave trade throughout the British Empire. Though he retired from Parliament due to failing health, he continued to campaign against the institution of slavery itself, dying just three days after the Slavery Abolition Act 1833 was assured passage through the House of Commons.
